criteria.text: With stream_detached set, an established WebSocket stream stays open and keeps echoing after a config reload that keeps its upstream. TestStreamDetachedSurvivesReload.
With stream_detached set, a reload that removes a stream's upstream closes only the streams of that upstream; streams on retained upstreams stay open. TestStreamDetachedClosesRemovedUpstream.
Without stream_detached, a reload closes upgraded streams, immediately or after stream_close_delay. TestStreamDefaultClosedOnReload.

stream_logs parses in the Caddyfile and JSON (skip_handshake, level, default DEBUG). skip_handshake suppresses the handshake access log entry, and the stream close log is emitted with logger_name access. TestStreamLogsConfig and TestDetachedStreamAccessLog.
After Hijack, the response recorder and the encode writer drop any WriteHeader or Write; a 101 is treated as final. TestResponseRecorderNoWriteAfterHijack, TestEncodeUpgradeFinal101.

A WebSocket upgrade works through the encode handler and through intercept with handle_response, and the proxy copies on the raw connection, not through the recorder's hijackedConn. TestUpgradeThroughEncode, TestUpgradeThroughIntercept.
HTTP/2 extended CONNECT WebSocket works over h2 with a real h2 client, and HTTP/1.1 upgrades work in detached mode. TestExtendedConnectH2, TestDetachedHTTP11Upgrade.
Metrics report active streams, closed streams by result, duration and bytes in each direction. Each stream is counted exactly once even when several close paths race. TestStreamMetricsAccountedOnce.

Caddyfile stream_detached and stream_logs { skip_handshake; level } parse into the Handler fields (StreamDetached, StreamLogs) and unknown subdirectives are rejected. TestUnmarshalCaddyfileStreamDetached in the reverseproxy package.
Doc comments for JSON fields and the Caddyfile syntax block describe stream_detached and stream_logs.
Unit tests cover the detached registry and its upstream-removal pruning, and the stream finish-once accounting. TestDetachedRegistryPrune, TestStreamFinishOnce.

intents.rationale: No stream_detached option exists. Streams are registered in per-Handler maps that Cleanup closes. A detached mode needs a registry that outlives the handler, plus a reload step that closes only streams whose upstream was removed.
The default must stay as is, so the existing cleanupConnections and close-delay path is kept for non-detached handlers. Regression tests pin it.

There is no stream_logs config and no stream close log tied to the access logger. Add a StreamLogs struct (skip_handshake, level), a stream close log entry, and a way to suppress the handshake access log entry.

The recording and encode writers can still write after a hijack. A 101 is not treated as final: the recorder's wroteHeader stays false for 1xx. The proxy also copies via the Hijack-wrapped conn, which counts bytes into the recorder.
Extended CONNECT (h2ReadWriteCloser) and HTTP/1.1 upgrade paths exist and must keep working. The detached registry must support both conn types, and tests must cover them.
metrics.go only has the upstreams_healthy gauge. Add active streams, closed-by-result counter, duration histogram and bytes counters, each stream recorded exactly once.
The new options need Caddyfile parsing, JSON fields and doc comments. The Caddyfile syntax doc block lists stream_close_delay and must gain the new subdirectives.
Integration tests are needed. stream_test.go exists and can be extended, and intercept_test.go can hold the intercept case.
Unit tests are needed for the registry, response writers, encode and Caddyfile parsing.

tasks.summary: Add stream_detached and stream_logs to reverse_proxy with a process-wide registry of detached streams that is pruned on reload by upstream. Add stream metrics with once-only accounting. Make response writers hijack-safe (no writes after hijack, 101 final, raw-conn copy). Caddyfile parsing is tested by a Go unit test in the reverseproxy package; no .caddyfiletest data file is added. Order of work: (1) config fields and Caddyfile parsing; (2) registry and metrics in streaming.go/metrics.go; (3) wire Provision/Cleanup; (4) writer fixes in responsewriter/encode/intercept and logging; (5) unit tests; (6) integration tests.
